Bring Your A-Game — AI Agent Idea

ShapeAI

From business intent to delivery-ready stories.

1What would you like to call your AI agent?

ShapeAI

2The problem

Turning a business idea into a development-ready user story takes more than writing a Jira ticket. Business Analysts spend time interpreting stakeholder intent, structuring requirements, identifying missing scenarios, defining acceptance criteria and preparing stories for refinement. Information can be fragmented across conversations, meeting notes, Jira and Confluence, while ambiguity or missed dependencies can lead to repeated clarification and rework during delivery. AI tools can generate stories, but the bigger opportunity is to improve the quality of thinking before engineering starts.

3The solution

ShapeAI is an AI Business Analysis Agent that turns business intent into validated, delivery-ready requirements. A BA can provide a rough idea, meeting notes, an existing story or requirements. ShapeAI identifies gaps, asks targeted questions instead of making assumptions, shapes the story and acceptance criteria, challenges it for edge cases, dependencies and non-functional requirements, and provides a Story Readiness assessment. The BA remains in control, reviews the output and can publish the approved story into Jira.

4What will your AI agent do?

✓ Receive information ✓ Understand and analyze information ✓ Generate content or recommendations ✓ Help make decisions or prioritize ✓ Execute tasks in systems ✓ Coordinate workflows and people ✓ Interact with and support users ✓ Monitor and support risk management ✓ Others
Other: Interview the BA to uncover missing requirements, challenge assumptions and edge cases, assess Story Readiness and prepare delivery-ready Jira stories.

8What type of value will this AI agent create?

✓ Knowledge access ✓ Task execution ✓ Automation ✓ Decision support ✓ Content creation ✓ Insights and analysis ✓ Innovation ✓ Capability building ✓ Experience enhancement ✓ Risk and governance ○ Others
Business value: Reduce the effort required to move from business intent to development-ready requirements, while improving consistency and identifying ambiguity, missing scenarios and dependencies before development begins. For an illustrative team delivering 5 stories per month, reducing BA preparation from 4.5 to 1.5 hours per story could release around 180 hours — approximately 24 working days — of BA capacity per year. At an illustrative £50/hour loaded cost, that is approximately £9,000 of BA capacity per team/year. If improved story quality also avoids only one hour of clarification across a BA, developer and tester per story, the combined illustrative opportunity is approximately £18,900 per team/year.
~67%Potential reduction in story preparation effort
180 hrsPotential BA capacity released per team/year
~24 daysPotential BA working days returned per team/year
~£18.9KIllustrative total opportunity per team/year
Measurement approach: These are business-case assumptions, not claimed savings. A pilot would baseline time-to-ready, preparation effort, refinement returns, clarification requests and requirement changes after sprint start to quantify actual benefits.

9How many people will benefit from the outcomes created by this agent?

More than 50 colleagues — BAs benefit directly, while Product Owners, Developers, Testers and delivery teams benefit from clearer, better-shaped requirements.
